cookieAuth.name: better-auth.session_token
cookieAuth.description: The sign-in session cookie of the web (`__Secure-` prefixed over https). Set by the web’s own sign-in, not by this contract.

bearerAuth.description: The token of `POST /v1/sign-in/token`: a sign-in session. Ended by `POST /v1/sign-out`.

NotSignedIn.description: The request has no valid sign-in session. Contains no user-facing text.

NotFound.description: The workspace or record does not exist or is out of the caller’s reach; the answer is the same for both. Contains no user-facing text.

Forbidden.description: The caller has a place in the workspace, but not the access this route needs. Contains no user-facing text.

HealthResponse.description: Liveness of the API and its dependencies. Contains no error details.

greetingKey.description: i18n message key that the client renders in `locale`.

Locale.description: Catalog locale from packages/i18n: Dutch (nl-NL) or English (en).

path.description: Dot-separated path of the invalid field.

ValidationError.description: The request did not match the contract. Contains no user-facing text.

email.description: The address the account signs in with.

name.description: The person’s own name; null until one is given (TW-11 asks for it).

preferredLocale.description: The language stored on the account; null until one is stored.

canCreateWorkspace.description: Whether the account may set up a workspace: it is on the sign-up allowlist and has no team role in any workspace yet. The web and the apps show the first-run screen or the no-access page from this, never from rules of their own.

workspaces.description: The workspaces the account has a team role in, by name. Empty when it has none. Workspaces it is only a client of are not listed.

name.description: The name shown in the product.

slug.description: The URL name: `/w/{slug}` on the web.

role.description: What the account is in the workspace; shown as a label, never decided on.

capabilities.description: What the account may do in the workspace, from the permission matrix. The web and the apps show a section or an action only when its capability is listed, never from the role name; the API refuses the rest with `403` anyway.

name.description: The person’s own name, as shown in every workspace they are on: trimmed, at least one and at most 80 characters. Empty, blank or longer answers `400` with a field error.

preferredLocale.description: The language to store on the account, for its screens and emails: `nl-NL` or `en`. Any other value, a browser’s `nl-BE` included, is refused with `400`.

surface.description: The app that sends the request: `ios` or `android`. A request with a bearer token that changes `preferredLocale` records the `language_changed` event with this surface; without it nothing is recorded. The web does not send it, and a request without a bearer token ignores it.

UpdateMeRequest.description: What to change on the signed-in account. Fields left out stay as they are.

SignInRequest.description: Asks for the sign-in email. `locale` is the interface language the app resolved; the email follows ADR-019.

token.description: The bearer token: a sign-in session, valid 30 days after its last use and renewed on use. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Unauthorized.description: The request has no valid sign-in session. Contains no user-facing text.

email.description: The address the account signs in with.

name.description: The name shown in the product.

slug.description: The URL name, made from the name when the workspace is created and never changed by a rename. Lower case letters, digits and hyphens.

timeZone.description: The IANA time zone dates and times are shown in, for example `Europe/Amsterdam`.

personName.description: The creator’s own name, stored on the account. Leave it out when the account has one.

name.description: The new name, as the product shows it from now on.

UpdateWorkspaceRequest.description: Changes a workspace: its name, its default communication language (the language of emails to people whose own preference is unknown, never what anyone sees on screen, ADR-017), or both. The slug stays, so links keep working. Other fields are ignored.

name.description: The client’s name: trimmed, at least one and at most 120 characters. Empty, blank or longer answers `400` with a field error.

email.description: The client’s email address; stored lower case. Leave it out to add the client with a name only. An address that is no email address answers `400`. If a client of the workspace has it already, nothing is added and the answer is `409`.

emailLocale.description: The language for the client’s emails: `nl-NL` or `en`. Leave it out to follow the workspace’s default language. Any other value answers `400`.

surface.description: The app that sends the request: `ios` or `android`. A request with a bearer token records the `client_added` event with this surface; without it nothing is recorded. The web does not send it, and a request without a bearer token ignores it.

AddClientRequest.description: A client to add. Only the name is required.

name.description: The new name: trimmed, at least one and at most 120 characters, as when adding. Leave it out to keep the name. Empty, blank or longer answers `400` with a field error.

email.description: The new email address; stored lower case. `null` clears it. Leave it out to keep it. An address that is no email address answers `400`; one that another client of the workspace has answers `409`. The client’s link to an account, if any, follows the address; the answer is the same either way, and the account itself never changes.

emailLocale.description: The new language for the client’s emails: `nl-NL` or `en`. `null` follows the workspace’s default language. Leave it out to keep it. Any other value answers `400`.

UpdateClientRequest.description: The fields of a client to change. Fields left out stay as they are.

get.description: The account of the sign-in session in the request. The web sends the sign-in session cookie, the apps’ `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (the token of `POST /v1/sign-in/token`). A request with an `Authorization` header is judged by that token alone, never by a cookie. It also tells where the person goes after sign-in: the workspaces they have a team role in, and whether they may set one up (`canCreateWorkspace`).

500.description: Unexpected server error, reported to error tracking. Contains no error details.

patch.description: Stores the language the person chose (`preferredLocale`), so every browser and app of the account shows it from its next load, and the name they gave themselves (`name`), one per account, shown in every workspace they are on. Answers with the account, as `GET /v1/me` does. A language other than `nl-NL` or `en`, or a name that is empty, blank or over 80 characters, answers `400` and nothing changes.

post.description: Sends the sign-in email (EM-08, a link and a 6-digit code) to an account or an allowed address. The answer is the same for every address and for a request over the rate limits, so it never says who has an account.

400.description: The request did not match the contract.

500.description: Unexpected server error, reported to error tracking. Contains no error details.

post.summary: Exchange the emailed code for a bearer token
post.description: Uses up the verification of the email (the web’s link and code are the same one), creates the account at the first sign-in of an allowed address, and returns a bearer token. It sets no cookie. Every failure gets the same 401.

400.description: The request did not match the contract.

401.description: The code was not accepted. Nothing says why: it can be wrong, used, replaced, expired or out of attempts, or this network asked too often.

500.description: Unexpected server error, reported to error tracking. Contains no error details.

post.description: Ends the sign-in session of the bearer token in the request, and only that one. Other phones and browsers of the account stay signed in.

204.description: The sign-in session has ended. The body is empty.

500.description: Unexpected server error, reported to error tracking. Contains no error details.

post.description: Creates a workspace and makes the caller its Owner, in one transaction: the workspace (Dutch as its default language, `Europe/Amsterdam`, a slug made from its name, with a number added when taken), the Owner’s team role and, when given, the account’s name. Only an account on the sign-up allowlist with no team role in any workspace may: anyone else gets `403` and nothing is created.

delete.description: Removes a person from the team of the workspace (the Owner only). Only the team access goes: the person’s account and sign-in sessions stay, and so does anything they have as a client of the workspace. It takes effect on the person’s next request. A workspace keeps at least one Owner: removing the last one answers `409` and changes nothing.

patch.description: Makes a team member of the workspace an Owner or a Trainer (the Owner only). The role is replaced on the same team-member record, so a person never has two roles in a workspace. It takes effect on the person’s next request. A workspace keeps at least one Owner: making the last Owner a Trainer answers `409` and changes nothing. A role other than `owner` or `trainer` (`admin` included) answers `400`.

post.description: Adds a client to the workspace (the Owner and every Trainer). Only the name is required. Adding a client never sends an email and never creates an account. If an account has the email address, the client is linked to it; the answer is the same either way. A client of the workspace with the same address (in any case) makes the answer `409` with that client’s ID, and nothing is added. Two clients without an email address may share a name.

patch.description: Changes the name, email address or language for emails of a client (the Owner and every Trainer); fields left out stay as they are. The rules of adding apply: a trimmed name of at most 120 characters, a valid email address stored lower case. The email address may be cleared with `null`. An address another client of the workspace has answers `409` with that client’s ID, and nothing changes. If the email address changes, the client’s link to an account follows it: to the account that has the new address, otherwise to none. The answer is the same either way, and the team never changes the account itself.
